title: Scaled Anatomical Model Creation of Biomedical Tomographic Imaging Data and Associated Labels for Subsequent Sub-surface Laser Engraving (SSLE) of Glass Crystals
protocol: Conduct micro X-ray computed tomography to generate a pre-clinical data set.
Image a bone core specimen using a microCT with settings of 45 kV, 0.4 mA, and 1,000 projections.
Reconstruct raw data at high resolution (125 µm isotropic voxel).
Identify and reconstruct a 1 cm cube with a center at the volume's origin for increased resolution (10 µm isotropic voxel).
Export reconstructed data set in DICOM format for additional processing.
Acquire reconstructed CT data sets from clinical collaborators or open-source DICOM archives.
Import files into DICOM imaging software and export as decompressed DICOM files if necessary.
Open each DICOM data set using the 'Load DICOM' function in the 'View' setting of the image processing software.
Save each data set as a NIfTI analyze format.
Import NIfTI files into a program for medical imaging computed and automated segmentation.
Upload a given NIfTI file into the surface map generator program with the 'Add Data' tool.
Select the 'Grayscale Model Maker' tool with the specification "Create and Rename new model".
Set lower threshold values to approximately 300 HU for the segmentation of bone.
Save grayscale models as STL files for further data processing.
Import each surface map into the 3D data preparation software (e.g., Netfabb Studio Basic).
Select 'Repair' mode.
Use the 'Select Part' and 'Delete' tools to delete all surfaces that do not represent the structure of interest.
Use the 'Add Triangle' tool to partially cover the holes in surfaces.
Use the 'Automatic Repair' script to completely close remaining gaps.
Select the 'Repair Degenerate Faces' script in the action menu to resolve edges without surface area.
Select the 'Apply Repair' script to exit 'Repair' mode with the modified part.
Use the 'Cut' tool to remove unwanted features or reduce the size of the model.
Designate the location of each cut within the 'X', 'Y', or 'Z' plane in the 'Cut' menu of the context area.
Use the 'Execute Cut' tool and choose 'Triangulate Cut' in the settings to automatically close all resulting holes.
Use the 'Select Part' and 'Delete' tools simultaneously to delete all surfaces resulting from the cut that do not represent the structure of interest.
Select the 'Create 2D Sketch' tool and choose any plane.
Use the 'Center Point Circle' tool in the 'Draw' menu of the toolbar to produce a circle with a center at the origin.
Use the 'Dimension' tool in the 'Constraint' menu to set the diameter of the circle (1.0 mm).
Select the 'Finish Sketch' option in the 'Exit' menu of the toolbar.
Select the 'Extrude' tool chosen from the 'Create' menu of the toolbar with the option '2D text'.
Select an extrusion depth (10.00 mm) with the symmetric setting.
Export text labels and cylinders in CAD format with the 'Save as Type' .stl setting.
Import models, text labels, and cylindrical label lines into the 3D data preparation software.
Translate text labels to the left or right of the associated anatomy using the 'Move Part' tool.
Use the 'Rotate Part' tool to orient labels such that they face the same direction.
Translate and rotate cylindrical label lines using the 'Move Part' and 'Rotate Part' tools to connect labels to associated structures within the model.
Enter 'Repair' mode and use the 'Select Triangles' and 'Remove Selected Triangles' to reduce the size of cylinders to the appropriate length.
Select all parts and save as a project in the basic version.
Reopen this project in the professional version.
Select all parts and export as a single STL.
Create a new workbook in the CAD program by selecting 'New' and 'Standard (mm).ipt' part.
Select 'Create 2D Sketch' and choose any of the three planes to begin working on.
Draw a rectangle with dimensions 10 mm x 0.25 mm using the 'Rectangle' tool.
Use the 'Dimension' tool to specify the width as 10 mm and the length as 0.25 mm.
Place the lower left vertex on the origin for ease of adding tick marks.
Draw a rectangle above the scale bar with dimensions 0.025 mm x 0.432 mm using the 'Rectangle' tool to create the first tick mark.
Use the 'Dimension' tool to constrain the size and position of the tick mark.
Translate the newly formed rectangle so it lies at 2.5 mm from the edge of the scale bar, creating a tick mark.
Repeat the process for additional tick marks spaced every 2.5 mm along the length of the scale bar.
Select the 'Rectangle' tool to create a square and constrain the length and width (2 mm x 2 mm) with the 'Dimension' tool.
Choose 'Finish Sketch' to return to the 3D Model setting.
Under 'Create', choose 'Extrude' and select the square drawn in 2D Sketch mode.
Enter an extrusion depth of 20 mm and select a direction (into the screen).
Select 'Create 2D Sketch' and continue working on the same plane as the previous sketch.
Use the 'Rectangle' and 'Dimension' tools to draw a rectangle (2 mm x 18 mm) directly above the square.
Press 'Finish Sketch' when completed.
Under 'Create', choose 'Extrude' and select the rectangle.
Enter an extrusion depth of 2 mm and select a direction (into the screen).
Rotate the part so that it looks like the letter 'L'.
Create a new 2D sketch and select the front of the 'L' as the working plane.
Draw a square at the corner of the two rectangles using the 'Rectangle' tool.
Constrain the dimensions (2 mm x 2 mm) so that it fits exactly in the corner.
Exit the sketch with the 'Finish Sketch' tool.
Choose 'Extrude' under 'Create,' and select the newly created square.
Enter an extrusion distance of 18 mm, choose a direction out of the screen, and apply the extrusion.
Create a new 2D sketch off of any plane.
Use the 'Text' tool in the 'Draw' menu to produce a label with Times New Roman font and size 2.5 mm.
Translate the text to its desired position next to the scale bar.
Exit sketch mode by selecting 'Finish Sketch'.
Utilize the 'Extrude' tool, enter an extrusion distance of 2 mm, and choose a direction that aligns the label with the scale bar into the screen.
Repeat steps using the other planes to create labels for all three axes.
Export the scale bar and its accompanying labels in CAD format with the '.stl' setting.
Open the anatomical model in the 3D data preparation software.
Import the scale bar.
Use the 'Move Part' tool to orient the scale bar next to the anatomical model.
Use the 'Rotate Part' tool to position the scale bar appropriately.
Import the part two more times.
Translate and rotate the individual scale bars so one lies on each axis.
Select all parts and save as a project if using the basic version.
Open the file in the professional version.
Select all parts and export as a single STL.
Utilize the 'Import Mesh' tool to add an .STL file in the 3D mesh-processing program.
Under 'Filters,' select 'Remeshing, Simplification and Reconstruction.'
Choose the 'Quadratic Edge Collapse Decimation' tool.
Enter the target number of faces (100,000).
Select 'Apply.'
Export the finished product as an STL using the 'Export Mesh As…' setting.
Open the STL file into a laser engraving software program.
Convert the STL file to a SCAX file.
Import the SCAX file in a software package connected to the 3D laser engraving machine.
Define an appropriate crystal size for interfacing with the SCAX file.
Set the power of the laser.
Enter a voltage and density, typically starting at 8.5 V and 0.2.
Adjust the voltage and density as needed to prevent cracking or breaking of the crystal.
Send the file to a 3D laser engraver for crystal production.
